title: No information transmission through quantum channels above capacity
abstract: We show that the capacity of a quantum channel demarcates a phase transition: while reliable transmission below capacity is always possible, any attempt to transmit information above it fails catastrophically. Specifically, we prove exponential strong converse theorems for unassisted quantum and classical communication over arbitrary finite-dimensional memoryless quantum channels. At rates beyond the respective capacity, the entanglement-generation fidelity and the success probability for classical communication decay exponentially with the number of channel uses. This rules out transmission above capacity even when one tolerates arbitrarily large errors. Our proof follows the classical Arimoto strategy, augmented by a crucial new ingredient: integral representations of Rényi information measures that lead to asymptotic continuity bounds for Rényi capacities.
summary: This paper rigorously proves exponential strong converse theorems for quantum and classical communication over arbitrary quantum channels. By utilizing integral representations of Rényi information, the authors demonstrate that any attempt to transmit information above the channel's capacity fails exponentially fast. This work provides fundamental, sharp limits on quantum information processing capabilities.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish an exponential strong converse theorem for information transmission through quantum channels, proving that communication rates exceeding the channel capacity fail catastrophically.
main_result: The authors prove that at rates beyond the quantum or classical capacity, the entanglement-generation fidelity and success probability decay exponentially with the number of channel uses.
method: The proof adapts the classical Arimoto strategy, crucially employing integral representations of Rényi information measures to establish asymptotic continuity bounds for Rényi capacities.
model_or_system: The analysis concerns arbitrary finite-dimensional memoryless quantum channels, considering both classical and quantum information transmission protocols.
key_observables: Capacity ($C$ or $Q$), entanglement-generation fidelity ($F_{eg}$), and the success probability for classical communication.
important_parameters: The Rényi order ($\alpha > 1$) and the transmission rate ($r$) relative to the capacity.
main_assumptions: The core technical steps involve bounding fidelity using the sandwiched Rényi divergence and adapting the Leung–Smith telescoping argument.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the asymptotic coding transition, distinguishing between weak converse (fixed error) and strong converse (error tending to one) behavior.
paper_structure: The structure builds from defining the problem (strong converse) to introducing the mathematical machinery (Rényi measures, integral representations), deriving the converse bounds for both quantum and classical settings, and finally proving the equivalence of various rate bounds.
why_interesting: The rigorous characterization of capacity limits via strong converse theorems provides fundamental, non-trivial bounds on what is physically possible for information processing using quantum resources.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. The asymptotic coding transition. Darker curves represent longer codes. Direct coding theorems drive the optimal error to zero below capacity, whereas a strong converse drives it to one above capacity. The corresponding exponents quantify the approach to the limiting step. No behavior at the transition point itself is asserted.
